lemma: Reduction (exact, for G = K_n, GF(3)): dim Ker F(K_n) = 2n, so H_B has k = 2n vertices. A graph H on k vertices has tw(H) = k-1 iff H is complete (non-adjacent u,v give a width k-2 decomposition with bags V-{v}, V-{u}). Hence min_B tw(H_B) = 2n-1 iff no two nonzero vectors of Ker F(K_n) have disjoint supports. The K_n part of (A) is therefore equivalent to a finite support statement. The owner's Lean identity implies it for GF(3); the check here is independent verification for n=3,4.

lemma: For n>=2 let F(K_n) over GF(3) have variables x_{v,c} (vertex v, colour c) and y_{uv,c} (edge uv, colour c), with rows sum_c x_{v,c}=0 for each v and x_{u,c}+x_{v,c}+y_{uv,c}=0 for each edge uv and colour c. Then dim Ker F(K_n)=2n, no two nonzero kernel vectors have disjoint supports, and hence every basis B gives H_B complete on 2n vertices, so tw(H_B)=2n-1=2*tw(K_n)+1 for every basis B and all n>=2.

proved_step: Proof: let z=(x,y), z'=(x',y') be nonzero with disjoint supports. (1) A nonzero vertex block x_v has support of size >=2, since its coordinates sum to 0 over GF(3). Two nonzero blocks x_v, x'_v cannot both occur, because two disjoint subsets of a 3-set of size >=2 do not exist. So the vertex sets A={v: x_v != 0} and A'={v: x'_v != 0} are disjoint. (2) Both are nonempty, since x=0 forces y=0. Pick a in A and b in A'; then x_b=0 and x'_a=0. (3) y_{ab,c}=-x_{a,c} in z, so it is nonzero iff c in supp(x_a); y'_{ab,c}=-x'_{b,c} in z', so it is nonzero iff c in supp(x'_b). Both sets have size >=2 inside {0,1,2}, so they meet at some c, giving a shared support coordinate. Contradiction. Dimension: vertex rows are independent and each edge row has a private y variable, so dim = 3n - n = 2n.
